newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Turkey gets EU consolation offer of closer ties.
newsitem.headline: Turkey gets EU consolation offer of closer ties.

text.p: The European Commission on Tuesday offered Turkey a consolation prize for not being invited into EU membership talks, calling for deeper links to be developed between Ankara and the soon-to-be enlarged bloc.
It said it wanted the European Union to go beyond the existing customs union with Turkey and offer assistance in areas ranging from agriculture to information technology.
Turkey could be given assistance to upgrade its agriculture, improve its investment climate and develop its telecoms sector, it said.

But the Commission also underlined that closer political and economic ties were linked to Turkey's protection of human rights, its good relations with neighbour Greece and a lasting settlement to the issue of divided Cyprus.
The call for closer links came as the Commission formally agreed to recommend that EU membership talks begin next year with Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Estonia and Slovenia.
The EU has previously agreed to begin talks with Cyprus.

EU relations with Turkey have been rocky for the past few years, in part because of its long-time rivalry with Greece, which held up the agreement on a customs union for years over fears of Turkish designs on its borders.

The customs union, a pact to open most of the EU's vast market to Turkish goods, eventually came into effect in December 1995 but has been hampered by a row over financing for Turkey to adjust to the new liberalisation.

Relations became particularly strained earlier this year when Christian Democrat leaders, including German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, appeared to rule out Turkish EU membership for ever on cultural grounds.

EU foreign ministers sought to undo the damage at a meeting in the Netherlands in April by stating that Turkey was eligible for EU membership in the long run and ordering the Commission to look into ways of strengthening ties.

As well as offering assistance on economic issues, the Commission also proposed on Tuesday that the EU and Turkey develop closer links in such areas as consumer policy, the environment, human rights and humanitarian affairs.
